SUCF canonical forms

Dual-target, zero-allocation canonical (de)composition over the full 64-bit SUCS space.

SUCF (SUAS-004) is the canonical-equivalence engine of SuperUnicode: a single-pass, zero-allocation sliding-window (de)composition engine over sucs_ex_char_t (a UAX #15 analog). Within the Unicode Bridge it reproduces Unicode canonical equivalence; in the native space it makes canonical treatment of SCP, Trap, Sentinel and native codepoints explicit.

Target Behavior
SUCF-C Canonical composition — the compact storage / equality form: decompose, reorder by CCC, recompose greedily.
SUCF-D Canonical decomposition — the analysis / stripping / sorting form: decompose and reorder, never recompose.
  • CCC reordering — marks sort ascending by Canonical Combining Class; swap iff CCC_A > CCC_B and CCC_B ≠ 0; stable for equal classes; starters never move.
  • Hangul — syllables 0xAC00–0xD7A3 decompose algorithmically (no table rows); SUCF-C composes L+V and LV+T arithmetically.
  • Composition exclusions — singletons (e.g. U+212B Å) and non-starter exclusions never recompose.
  • SCP immunity — SCP 0x00110000–0x0011FFFF, BANcodes, Trap and Sentinel pass through untouched and never disturb combining state.
  • Stream-safe — 30 non-starters per run; quick check returns YES/NO/MAYBE; streaming equals bulk transform.

Formalized in SUAS-004. Source of truth: docs/suas/SUAS-004-sucf.md.
